name: Daptomycin
route: IV infusion or 2-minute IV injection, once a day (adults)
status: FDA-approved for complicated skin infections (2003) and S. aureus bloodstream infections (2006); generics available
mechanism: With calcium, inserts into Gram-positive bacterial membranes and seizes cell-wall building blocks, collapsing the membrane and killing the cell
uses: Complicated skin and skin structure infections

article.summary: Daptomycin (Cubicin) is a once-daily IV antibiotic for serious skin infections and Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections, including MRSA. It is not used for pneumonia.
article.takeaway: Daptomycin was the first of a class called cyclic lipopeptides, made by a soil bacterium. It kills Gram-positive bacteria, including **MRSA** and many vancomycin-resistant strains, and is given as a single daily IV dose. It matched standard antibiotics in large trials for complicated skin infections and for S. aureus bloodstream infections.[^1][^2] Lung surfactant inactivates it, so it does not work for pneumonia.[^3] The main safety watch-points are **muscle injury**, tracked with weekly blood tests, and a rare allergic lung reaction.[^4]
glance: Approved 2003 (skin infections) and 2006 (S. aureus bloodstream infections); generics available
Complicated skin infections; S. aureus bacteremia including right-sided endocarditis
Once daily IV; 7-14 days for skin infections, 2-6 weeks for bloodstream infections
Pneumonia or left-sided heart valve infections

blocks.text: Daptomycin is a chain of 13 amino acids, mostly closed into a ring, with a fatty-acid tail. It was originally isolated from Streptomyces roseosporus, a soil bacterium. In the presence of calcium, it inserts into the outer membrane of Gram-positive bacteria. Research published in 2020 showed it clusters at the site where the cell divides, grabbing carrier-bound cell-wall building blocks along with membrane lipids.[^5] Wall construction stalls, the membrane is rearranged and leaks, and the bacterium dies quickly.

Because Gram-negative bacteria have a different outer envelope, daptomycin has no useful activity against them. It is also neutralized by surfactant, the fatty coating inside the lungs, which is why it failed in a pneumonia trial despite working well elsewhere.[^3]

rows: Clinical success 83.4% vs 84.2% with penicillins or vancomycin; more patients finished in 4-7 days[^1]
246 adults with bloodstream infection, with or without endocarditis
Success 44.2% vs 41.7% with standard therapy; kidney problems 11% vs 26%[^2]

blocks.text: The bacteremia trial also showed a weakness: some patients whose infection persisted developed bacteria with reduced sensitivity to daptomycin.[^2] Clinicians often use higher-than-label doses for difficult infections, a practice based on observational data rather than the label.

Adults receive 4 mg/kg once daily for 7-14 days for complicated skin infections, or 6 mg/kg once daily for 2-6 weeks for S. aureus bloodstream infections. It can be infused over 30 minutes or, in adults, pushed over 2 minutes, which makes it practical for home IV therapy. People with poor kidney function get the dose every 48 hours instead. Children aged 1-17 receive age-based doses as an infusion.[^4]

items: **Muscle:** creatine kinase (CPK) rises, muscle pain and, rarely, rhabdomyolysis; CPK is checked weekly and statins are often paused during treatment[^4]
**Eosinophilic pneumonia:** a rare allergic lung reaction with fever, cough and breathlessness; most cases improve quickly once the drug is stopped[^6]
**Other serious reactions:** anaphylaxis, DRESS (a severe drug rash with organ involvement), kidney inflammation, peripheral nerve symptoms and C. difficile diarrhea[^4]
**Common:** diarrhea, headache, dizziness, rash and abnormal liver tests

blocks.text: It is avoided in babies under 12 months because of muscle and nerve effects seen in newborn animal studies.[^4]

Daptomycin was approved in 2003 for complicated skin infections and in 2006 for S. aureus bloodstream infections, including right-sided endocarditis. Pediatric approvals for ages 1-17 followed. Cubicin RF is a room-temperature-stable version, and generic daptomycin is widely available.[^4]

evidence.label: Strong: randomized trials against standard therapy
evidence.text: Randomized trials involving more than 1,300 patients showed daptomycin performed as well as standard antibiotics for skin and S. aureus bloodstream infections.[^1][^2] Its failure in pneumonia is equally well documented and explained.[^3]

faq.a: Lung surfactant binds and inactivates it, so it cannot reach effective levels in the air sacs.[^3]

faq.q: Why do I need weekly blood tests on daptomycin?
faq.a: To check creatine kinase, a marker of muscle damage. Muscle injury is the drug's best-known serious side effect, and catching it early lets the team stop treatment in time.[^4]
Not overall: trials showed similar results.[^2] It is often chosen when vancomycin is failing, poorly tolerated, or the bacteria are less sensitive to vancomycin.

faq.q: Can it be given at home?
faq.a: Yes. Once-daily dosing and a short injection time make it common in home and outpatient IV programs, with regular blood monitoring.
